title: Electric Charges and Fields

standard_code: Class 12 Physics, Chapter 1: Electric Charges and Fields
standard_text: Electric charges, conservation of charge, Coulomb's law – force between two point charges, forces between multiple charges; superposition principle and continuous charge distribution. Electric field, electric field due to a point charge, electric field lines, electric dipole, electric field due to a dipole, torque on a dipole in uniform electric field. Electric flux, statement of Gauss's theorem and its applications to find field due to infinitely long straight wire, uniformly charged infinite plane sheet and uniformly charged thin spherical shell.

body_html:
How to think about it

Charge is quantised (q = ne, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) and conserved. Coulomb's law gives the force F = kq₁q₂/r² with k = 1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻². The electric field E = F/q is kq/r² for a point charge; field lines start on positive and end on negative charges.

A dipole has moment p = q × 2a; in a uniform field it feels no net force but a torque pE sin θ. Gauss's law says the flux through a closed surface is q/ε₀, giving E = λ/2πε₀r for a long wire and σ/2ε₀ for a plane sheet.

Example

2 μC and 3 μC, 0.3 m apart?

9 × 10⁹ × 6 × 10⁻¹² ÷ 0.09

Answer: 0.6 N

Example

Flux from 1 μC in a cube?

q/ε₀

Answer: 1.13 × 10⁵ N m²/C

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to square r.
  • Leaving μC unconverted.
  • Thinking the cube's size changes the flux.
